❓ Frequently asked questions

What DPI should I use for printing photos?

300 DPI is the standard for sharp photographic prints. 150 DPI is the practical minimum for close viewing; below that, prints look soft or pixelated.

How do I calculate print size from pixels?

Print size = pixels ÷ DPI. A 6000 × 4000 px image at 300 DPI prints at 20 × 13.3 inches.

Why is 150 DPI acceptable for posters but not small prints?

Very large prints (posters, banners) are viewed from far away, so 100–150 DPI can still look fine. This tool flags quality relative to close-up viewing.
